title: Microsoft president: AI is less regulated than milk
dek: Microsoft's president contrasted AI's risk to hacking with the stricter rules applied to milk.
body:
Microsoft's president said that artificial intelligence is less regulated than a carton of milk. He argued that milk cannot hack companies or governments the way AI can, yet milk faces stricter regulation than AI does.

## Why it matters

A senior executive at one of the world's largest tech companies publicly compared the regulatory environment for AI to that for a common food product. The comparison frames AI not just as a technology but as a potential source of harm to institutions , including cyber intrusions — and suggests current oversight is lagging.

The remark puts pressure on policymakers and industry to explain why a product that can enable hacks is subject to lighter regulation than a widely regulated consumer good. It also signals that major tech firms are aware of regulatory gaps and are drawing public attention to them.

## The details

- The statement came from Microsoft’s president.
- He said AI can hack companies and governments, whereas a carton of milk cannot.
- He claimed milk is subject to more regulation than AI.
- The available reporting does not specify where or when the comments were made.
- The available reporting does not include the president’s name or any follow-up policy proposals from Microsoft.
- The available reporting does not list specific regulations or regulatory bodies being compared.

## What to watch

Look for follow-ups from Microsoft clarifying the context, naming specific regulatory gaps, and proposing changes. Watch for government responses or policy proposals that reference the comparison between AI oversight and food-safety rules.
